title: The rendered formula in the tap keeps the template's header, which says it is never installed from and holds placeholders
body:
The rendered formula in the tap keeps the template's header. That header says the file is never installed from and that its tag and revision are placeholders, but brew installs from exactly this file, with the real tag and revision.

dc's from-brew walk of 0.1.15 (2026-10-27) ran each step as a plain brew user under `env -i`, with a scratch HOME (~/Devel/scratch/devbin-dc/walk015/run-20261027-0916Z/: findings.md, and steps/<id>.{out,err,rc}). vc measured each finding against that record and main at 15f2a973.

## Measured

Steps 003 and 004: the tap's Formula/devbin.rb, byte-identical to the keg's .brew copy, opens with packaging/homebrew/devbin.rb's header (lines 1-11): "It is never installed from this file ... The tag and the revision below are placeholders that render fills".

## Fix

`formula render` writes a header of its own for the rendered file and drops the template's. That header says the file was rendered from devbin's template for that tag, and that edits go into the template, not this file.

## Done when

1. A rendered formula's header names its tag and says it was rendered from the template, with none of the template's "never installed" or "placeholders" text. formula.bats holds it.
2. The landing suite passes under BSD and GNU with the tree scans and help, and CI is green on the pushed head.

## Resolution

0257 is fixed by fec41946 (tree 991dfaa5), one commit on fe0bb6c2. Its tree is the tree the landing run tested, bank 99158300.

### What changed, against "Done when"

1. **[x] A rendered formula's header names its tag and says it was rendered from the template, with none of the template's "never installed" or "placeholders" text. formula.bats holds it.**
   - lib/cmd/formula:
     - `template_split` splits a template at its header, the leading run of `#` comment and blank lines, read under the C locale, with a CRLF blank line counted as blank. A `=begin` block is no part of the header.
     - The header is dropped, and only the body is validated and filled. So a placeholder written in the header is neither counted nor filled, and a template with nothing after its header is refused. vc approved this widening of the issue.
     - A Ruby magic comment in the header stays at the top, with the blank line after it that Homebrew's style asks for. So does an Emacs mode line, or an encoding named on the first line.
     - `rendered_text` writes the file in one printf: the kept magic comments, then the render's own header, then the filled body. It does this in source and assets mode alike, for the cask too.
     - The header reads "RENDERED by devbin's formula built-in from the template below, for the tag below and the commit it names: edit the template, not this file, which the next render replaces". It then names the template, the tag and the commit.
     - The template is named from the project root, an absolute `formula.template` without its leading slashes, so no machine path reaches the tap (vc's R1).
   - lib/pages/formula.md gains "The rendered file's header": what it says, what of the template's is dropped and what is kept. Source mode's placeholder rule now reads "Below its header".
   - The arms are all in formula.bats:
     - the render's header over the template's body, byte for byte, the template's own phrases asserted present first (0195's arm, changed);
     - the magic comments kept in their order, around a decoy that reaches the key check, with one after the decoy and the blank line;
     - a CRLF template's header dropped, and its body kept byte for byte;
     - a placeholder in the header neither counted nor filled, and a template whose pins sit only there, or with nothing after its header, refused, writing nothing;
     - an absolute template named from the project root;
     - the assets render's formula and cask each under the render's header (0227's arm, changed).
   - Each arm reads its expected text with its own awk (`template_body`) and a literal header (`want_header`), not with the built-in's code.
2. **[x] The landing suite passes under BSD and GNU with the tree scans and help.** CI on the pushed head is vc's landing to read.

### The critic review

- The critic-shell subagent reviewed the first bank, 81aea747 against 617b155c: 0 critical, 3 warnings, 8 recommendations and 1 style point. vc approved the settled bank, 99158300.
  - **WARNING (CRLF):** `[[:blank:]]` did not read a CRLF blank line as blank, so a CRLF template kept every header paragraph after its first blank line. Both the code and the arms' oracle now use `[[:space:]]`, and an arm holds it.
  - **WARNING (Homebrew style):** kept magic comments sat directly above the render's header, which rubocop's Layout/EmptyLineAfterMagicComment flags. A blank line now follows them.
  - **WARNING (red-control):** the arm's decoy never reached the key allowlist. It is now `# Note: rendered`, which passes the shape check and fails the key check.
  - **Recommendations taken:**
    - an Emacs mode line, and line 1's `coding[:=]` form, are kept;
    - the split reads under the C locale;
    - a `=begin` block is named in the comment and the page as no part of the header;
    - one printf writes the file, since replace_file runs it where errexit is off;
    - the header is split off first, and only the body is validated and filled;
    - "Ruby reads most of them only before the first code", in place of "the only place Ruby reads one";
    - the source arm asserts the template's phrases before refuting them in the render;
    - a magic comment sits after the decoy and the blank line.
  - **Style taken:** "each file that render writes opens with a header of its own, below any magic comment it keeps".
  - **Not taken:** none.
- **The critic leg** ran `intent critic shell` on lib/cmd/formula and exited 0. It is the first critic leg since Intent's move to 3.2.6. Its coverage line reads as it did before the move: 2 of 6 rules asked, 4 declared unanswerable, and no shell findings at warning or above.

### Which arms are red on main, and which hold unchanged behaviour

- **Red on main:** all six 0257 arms, for the issue's reason:
  - the render opens with the template's header, "never installed" and placeholders included;
  - the magic comments are not kept above a render header;
  - the CRLF template's header ships;
  - the header's placeholders are counted: "the template holds 2 tag placeholder(s) and 2 revision placeholder(s)";
  - no header names the template;
  - the assets render's formula opens with no header of its own.
- **Two existing arms changed:** 0195's render arm and 0227's assets arm. Each is red on main for the issue's reason and green at the tip.
- **No arm holds unchanged behaviour.**

### Evidence

- **Red on fe0bb6c2**, red clone 10bab8dd (main with the arms alone), BSD, 2026-10-27 12:26:00Z by the driver's date -u: every 0257 arm fails as above.
- **Arm greens** at 99158300: BSD at 12:26:04Z and GNU at 12:26:11Z.
- **The light** at 99158300, on molt-vc's GO, slot 01M5YH4M54B4Y6BN3K1MK8BZSW. It started at 12:25:51Z, the driver exited 0 at 12:46:04Z, and the slot was released at 12:47:02Z, all by date -u.
  - formula (32 tests), releasecut (139) and help (57) were run whole under BSD and GNU, and every test passed. documentation (26) passed under BSD.
  - The tree scans ran under GNU, and every test passed: helpers (114), contract (42), neutral (10), documentation (26), readonlygit (11), harness (34), vendoredmd (3), workroom (5) and installhints (1). harness's two expected-skip arms skip, as they are written to.
  - Logs are in ~/Devel/scratch/devbin-dc/0257/runs/.
- **The bundle** 0257.bundle holds land-0257 at fec41946 and needs fe0bb6c2. It was verified in a fresh clone of canon: the fetched tree, 991dfaa5, is the tested tip's.
- **One transition effect, from the critic, not a defect:** a tap rendered before this lands differs from a new render by its header. So the first publish of a release already in the tap pushes a header-only commit, with the same `<name> <version>` message.
- **The landing:** vc landed it at `f3cbab33` as run; its paths equal the tested tip's; the BSD and GNU full suites run once before the cut, and CI reads the pushed head.

- **CI:** run 40523720517 on the pushed head 3f74c7f3, which carries the landing, read green by vc.
